foreign.comment: spec/reserved-words.md — keywords imported from another language. Marked INVALID on purpose: the editor shows the mistake before the compiler does. `use` was in this list and is a Heroes keyword, so every module line in every file showed as an error; it now sits in #keyword, where the spec puts it (`a module is named with use`). The list is otherwise the spec's own table, word for word.
foreign.name: invalid.illegal.foreign-keyword.hero

keyword.comment: spec/reserved-words.md's closing paragraph, and selfhost/keywords.hero::keyword. `true` and `false` were filed under #builtin-type, which is where a value is not: both tables call them keywords.
keyword.name: keyword.control.hero

builtin-type.comment: spec/heroes-spec.md § Types, the whole table. This read `int|f64|bool|str|ptr|cstr` and so coloured a word the language does not have while leaving every sized integer plain: `i64` is what a program actually writes, and it was the one type never highlighted. `[T]`, `{K: V}` and `T?` are shapes rather than words and are built out of these.
builtin-type.name: support.type.hero

hole.comment: `???` is a valid expression, not an error (§4.16)
hole.name: markup.italic.hole.hero

patterns.comment: spec § 2: five in a string, `\n` `\t` `\r` `\\` `\"`. This read `[nt\\"]` and said `exactly these four` until 2026-09-13, so a legal `\r` fell through to the rule below and a CORRECT program was painted `invalid.illegal`. Measured the day it was fixed: `print("a\rb")` runs at exit 0. `spec/heroes-spec.md:39` and `selfhost/escape.hero`'s `escape_text` are the two sides the `spec/colouring` check now holds together.
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.hero

patterns.comment: panel 192's R5: a character a line cannot show (a control character, a bidirectional control, U+2028 or U+2029) is written by its code, `\u{1b}`, in lowercase hexadecimal with no leading zero, its one spelling, of a code that names a character: a Unicode scalar value, never a surrogate (d800 to dfff) and nothing past 10ffff, which the compiler refuses as no escape (until 2026-10-07 this painted both, defect 377). Which characters a string must write by code is the compiler's to say (`selfhost/code_escape.hero`), so this paints every such code in the one spelling as an escape, and every other spelling falls to the rule below, as the compiler refuses it. The alternatives are by count of digits: one to three, four outside the surrogates, five, and six from 10
patterns.name: constant.character.escape.hero

patterns.comment: the backslash is reserved — anything else is a compile error
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.unknown-escape.hero

interpolated.comment: spec § 2: an `f` touching the opening quote makes `{e}` a hole, any expression, ended by the `}` that closes it with nested brackets and literals skipped; `{{` and `}}` each write one brace, and a `}` alone in the text is an error (panel 184 R1, ratified 2026-10-01). This grammar had no rule for the form until 2026-10-02 (`.claude/rules/diagnostics-and-goldens.md` measured it so on 2026-09-10), so a hole's code was painted as text and a quote inside a hole ended the string. The `spec/colouring` check holds the two brace escapes and the lone brace against what the compiler's own lexer accepts and refuses (`selfhost/lex_interp.hero`).
interpolated.name: string.quoted.double.interpolated.hero

interpolation-hole.comment: A hole of an `f` literal: ordinary code up to the `}` that closes it, its content `meta.embedded` so a theme paints it as code rather than as the string around it, a `{ }` inside it (a map literal) taken whole so its `}` closes nothing early, and a literal inside it read as the literal it is, through `$self`.
interpolation-hole.name: meta.interpolation.hero

char.comment: one ASCII character or one escape; its value is an int (§4.3). The escape class carried `[nt\\']` until 2026-09-13 and so painted `'\r'` as `invalid.illegal.char-literal.hero` by falling through to the third pattern — the same missing `r` as in the string rule above, in the second of the two places it had to be written by hand.
